elements.text: An encoder-decoder model splits the problem in two. The encoder reads the whole input sequence and compresses what it understood into a fixed representation; the decoder reads that representation and writes the output sequence one token at a time. Nothing forces the two halves to share an architecture, which is why the pattern outlived the recurrent networks it was invented for.

elements.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class Decoder(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab, hidden):
        super().__init__()
        self.embed = nn.Embedding(vocab, hidden)
        self.rnn = nn.GRU(hidden, hidden, batch_first=True)
        self.out = nn.Linear(hidden, vocab)

    def forward(self, tokens, state):
        # tokens: (batch, time) of the PREVIOUS true tokens.
        x = self.embed(tokens)
        h, state = self.rnn(x, state)
        return self.out(h), state


def train_step(model, batch, opt, pad_id):
    loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(ignore_index=pad_id)
    logits, _ = model(batch.inputs, batch.state)
    loss = loss_fn(
        logits.reshape(-1, logits.size(-1)),
        batch.targets.reshape(-1),
    )
    opt.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
    opt.step()
    return loss.item()

elements.text: Clip the gradients. Recurrent decoders explode without it, and the failure looks like a bad learning rate for a long time before you find it.

elements.walkthrough: A model trained only with teacher forcing has never once seen its own mistake as input. The first wrong token at inference puts it in a state it was never trained on, and the rest of the sentence drifts.

elements.title: Why greedy is not enough
items: A locally best token can strand the rest of the sentence
No way to recover from an early mistake
Beam search keeps k hypotheses instead of one

elements.text: Beam search is the usual answer, and it is worth remembering that it is still an approximation — the true argmax over whole sequences is intractable, so every decoder in production is making a guess about which partial guesses to keep.

points: Greedy takes the best token, not the best sentence
Beam search keeps k candidates alive
Both are approximations of an intractable search
